thread:
Priya: FYI support escalation from ACME — embeddings throughput tanked this morning. Customer sees ~80% drop in vectors/sec but tokens/sec looks steady. Error rate up for batch endpoints.

Maya: putting customer case link here: https://support.example/acme/CASE-4421 — they attached logs and perf traces. They say it started after a model rotation last night.

Alex: can you paste the exact error they see? dimension mismatch or 400s?

Priya: main issues: some 400s with message "invalid_vector_dim", and intermittent 503s with "queue timeout". From their logs: `requested_dim=1536, model_dim=1536` for successful calls, but failing ones show `requested_dim=1536, model_dim=1024` — seems like a model variant mismatch?

Kevin: thanks — that smells like routing to a wrong model shard/variant. We had a gradual rollout of a smaller quantized variant last night (canary). Autoscaler also applied a burst policy at 03:20 UTC.

perf-bot: metric update — embeddings.vectors_per_sec (acme-org) dropped from 12k -> 2.3k between 03:18-03:30 UTC. gpu_utilization increased from 40% -> 92% at 03:25 UTC. queue_depth spiked to 750.

Alex: gpu util up while vectors/sec down = potential small-batch overhead or tiny model variant causing more per-vector computation? Or KV cache thrash causing more mem copies. Need to check batch sizing and model variant mapping.

Maya: customer reports they switched from async batching client to sync calls yesterday because of a client-side change. Could be higher req/sec with smaller batch sizes.

Priya: repro plan from support side: 1) hit endpoint with same payloads as customer; 2) vary client concurrency and batch settings; 3) capture model variant returned header X-Model-Variant; 4) gather gpu metrics.

Alex: I'll add a quick script to simulate. Example curl they used:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": ["...text..."], "model": "embed-large", "batch_size": 1}'
```

Alex: also check headers in responses for model variant: `x-redwood-model` and `x-redwood-variant`. If the variant shrunk dims, we'd see mismatch.

Kevin: checked routing logs for the canary pool. Around 03:22 UTC an autoscaler event moved 20% of traffic to canary-quant. Canary variant is 1024-dim to save memory. Looks like policy mis-flagged some dedicated requests as eligible for canary.

Priya: ah — that explains invalid_vector_dim. Why would tokens/sec be steady but vectors/sec drop?

Alex: vectors/sec is downstream of postprocessing. If many requests hit a 1024-dim variant but client expects 1536 vectors, they either get rejected (400) or we pad/truncate and still cost more GPU cycles due to extra conversions. Also smaller variants may not be able to sustain same per-second throughput with current batching settings — more overhead per request leads to lower vectors/sec.

Kevin: queue_depth spike suggests the front-line router buffered requests waiting for worker capacity. At high gpu_util, throughput flattens. We also saw an increase in small-batch calls (batch_size=1), which reduces batching efficiency.

Maya: customer says they didn't change model param; they did change client concurrency though. So two hits: wrong routing to canary variant + client-side smaller batches.

Alex: next steps (I'll run):
- repro locally hitting exact variant mix (simulate 20% canary).
- run with batch_size 1, 4, 16 to show vectors/sec delta.
- capture per-GPU kernel latencies and nvprof sampler.

Kevin: I'll roll back canary routing policy to strict model/version pin for ACME while we investigate. Also bump autoscaler thresholds to prevent oscillation.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued by Kevin — job id: rb-20260315-77, target: canary-routing-policy, initiated by Kevin.

perf-bot: quick numbers from staging replay:
- batch_size=16 -> vectors/sec ~11.6k, gpu_util=65%
- batch_size=4 -> vectors/sec ~6.1k, gpu_util=78%
- batch_size=1 -> vectors/sec ~2.1k, gpu_util=92%

Alex: that matches customer delta. Also saw 400s when request landed on 1024 variant.

Priya: customer-facing note: we should advise them to pin model version for now and revert client to async batching. I'll draft a message after rollback.

Maya: drafting: "We're rolling back a canary routing change that caused some requests to hit a reduced-dimension variant. For immediate mitigation, please pin model to 1536-dim 'embed-large@v12' and re-enable async batching (batch_size >=4). We're happy to help test."

Kevin: rollback completed — canary routing removed for ACME. Monitoring for 10m.

perf-bot: post-rollback metrics (03:42 UTC): vectors_per_sec recovered to 11.9k, gpu_util back to 68%, queue_depth down to 35. Error rate for invalid_vector_dim -> 0.

Priya: customer updated: throughput is back to normal, thanks. We'll keep thread open 24h for any regressions.

Alex: follow-ups: add a routing assert so requests with explicit model pin never route to variants with mismatched dims. Also add a metric emit when variant_dim != requested_dim to aid quicker detection.

Kevin: will add an automated guard in the router config and a rollout checklist step for verifying dim compatibility.

Maya: marking CASE-4421 resolved pending 24h watch. :white_check_mark:

Priya: thanks everyone — good cross-team response.
